lines.trans: Did you seriously come all the way here just to pick up an umbrella?
I came to kill two birds with one stone—pick up the umbrella and tell you something.
Go ahead, I will listen. By the way, what is in that bag?
Oh, these are sweet pancakes.
Hand them over, since you brought them thoughtfully.

words.gloss: since it is a thoughtful gift

lines.trans: Oh, you cannot have these. They already belong to someone else.
I bought the exact count requested: five green-tea and five plain.
Forget it. I was only saying that casually.
I was hoping you might join as a cast member for the new season of 2 Days and 1 Night.
I understand very well why your team needs me.
But why would I need that program?
I found many cases where top stars actually gained far more fans after starting a variety show.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

meanings.note: Sino-Korean term.

examples.trans: Since it's raining, please use an umbrella.
I lost my umbrella.

meanings.note: Used for gifts, money, messages, or documents.

examples.trans: I received a birthday present.
Please answer the phone.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.
I understand well (combining two errands).
Today is a (combining two errands) busy day.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of 주다, used when giving to elders or superiors.

examples.trans: I gave a present to my grandmother.
May I ask you a question?

meanings.en: words, remarks (humble when referring to one's own speech to a superior)
meanings.note: Used in 말씀을 드리다 ('to tell/inform a superior').

meanings.en: words, speech (honorific when referring to a superior's speech)

examples.trans: I spoke to the teacher.
Thank you for your kind words.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.
I want to I will listen right now.
How about trying to I will listen together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?
Did you hear about this sweet filled pancakes?
I was busy today because of sweet filled pancakes.

meanings.note: Used for giving things to someone of equal or lower status.

examples.trans: I gave a gift.
Please give me some water.

정성.gloss: since it is a thoughtful gift

meanings.en: since it is a thoughtful gift

examples.trans: Did you hear about this since it is a thoughtful gift?
I was busy today because of since it is a thoughtful gift.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.
Did you hear about this owner?
I was busy today because of owner.

meanings.note: Used when doing something independently or in a separate location.

examples.trans: We live separately.
We'll pay separately.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
Did you hear about this exact number?
I was busy today because of exact number.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2
I want to because we cannot match right now.
How about trying to because we cannot match together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Past tense is 샀다 / 샀어요.

examples.trans: I bought fruit at the mart.
I need to buy a birthday present for my friend.
Did you hear about this green tea?
I was busy today because of green tea.
There are five here.
Altogether, it is five people.

meanings.note: General-purpose counter noun used with native Korean determiners (한 개, 두 개, 세 개).

examples.trans: How many do you need?
I bought three loaves of bread.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: in expressions like 뭔 소리야? ('what are you talking about?')
audible sound made by people or things

examples.trans: Suddenly a strange sound was heard.

examples.text: 말도 안 되는 소리 하지 마.
examples.trans: Don't talk nonsense.
Did you hear about this Ms.?
I was busy today because of Ms..
Did you hear about this 1 night?
I was busy today because of 1 night.
Did you hear about this 2 days?
I was busy today because of 2 days.
It really is new compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is new and nice.

meanings.en: season (of a TV show or sports league)
meanings.note: Loanword from English 'season'.

examples.trans: The new season starts next month.
Last season was really fun.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'member', commonly used for regular cast members of variety shows or teams

examples.trans: A new member joined.
All our team members gathered.

meanings.note: literal spatial meaning
polite or indirect reference to the listener's group

examples.text: 그쪽에서 사전 녹화 좀 떠주면 안 되냐?
examples.trans: Couldn't your side pre-record them for us?
How are things on your side?

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Korean expresses 'need' as an adjective ('is needed by me').

examples.trans: I need help.
I need time.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: colloquial clipping of 프로그램
clipping of 프로페셔널

examples.trans: What shows are you watching these days?
That show has high viewership ratings.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Short for 연예 오락; used for television variety programs.

examples.trans: On weekends I watch variety shows with my family.
That actor is also very popular on variety shows.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'program'
software or planned sequence of events

examples.trans: There are many fun variety shows these days.
I am planning a new show.

meanings.note: used both transitively and intransitively

examples.trans: The meeting is starting soon.
I started studying Korean.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.
I understand well (on the contrary).
Today is a (on the contrary) busy day.

meanings.note: Used before adjectives or verbs.

examples.trans: Please give me a little more.
It's further away.

meanings.en: to be many, numerous, or abundant
meanings.note: Used for both countable and uncountable nouns.

examples.trans: Because it's the weekend, there are many people at the department store.

examples.text: 오늘 해야 할 일이 너무 많다.
examples.trans: There is too much work to do today.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'fan', used for admirers of singers, actors, or sports teams.

examples.trans: I'm a longtime fan of Cindy.
Fans are waiting in front of the waiting room.
Let's secured, won together today.
I worked hard to secured, won yesterday too.

meanings.note: Slightly more formal/deferential variant of 네, commonly used when speaking to a boss or superior.

examples.trans: Yes, understood.
Yes, I will prepare it right away.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
